Subject: 8080/tcp
Title: Port 8080 is already in use
Description: Service "orders-api" publishes port 8080/tcp on every host address, and that binding is already held on this host by python3 (pid 737076), listening on port 8080/tcp on 0.0.0.0.
Why it matters: The container will fail to start: the engine cannot bind a port another process already holds. On a deployment that stops the old stack first, the failure lands after the old one is already down.
What to do: Publish a different host port for "orders-api", or stop whatever currently holds 8080 before deploying.

Title: There is no way back from this deployment
Description: The rollback plan for this host is incomplete. Missing: proxy-config: apache configuration under /etc/httpd is not copied anywhere by this audit; take a copy before changing it, since a proxy that fails to start takes every site on this host down, not only the new one; snapshot: whether a hypervisor or provider snapshot of this host exists cannot be seen from inside it — confirm with whoever runs the infrastructure before deploying.
Why it matters: Every other finding in this report is about whether the deployment will work. This one is about what happens when it does not, and it is the only one that cannot be fixed after the fact.
What to do: Before deploying: note the image digests currently running, copy the web server configuration somewhere outside this host, and take a snapshot or a volume backup.

Subject: docker
Title: docker is installed but did not answer
Description: The docker binary is present, but querying the engine failed: docker is installed but its daemon could not be queried (docker exited 1: failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///nonexistent/docker.sock; check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running: dial unix /nonexistent/docker.sock: connect: no such…); the container, network, volume and image lists are unknown rather than empty. The usual cause is an unprivileged audit: /var/run/docker.sock is readable by root and the docker group only — re-run as root, or as a member of that group, for the container checks. Every check that compares the manifest against existing containers, networks, volumes and images was therefore skipped.
Why it matters: This is the honesty case that matters most in this section: with the engine unreachable, an empty conflict list means nothing was looked at, not that nothing is in the way.
What to do: Re-run the audit as a user who can reach the engine socket (root, or a member of the docker group) to get the conflict checks.

Subject: nginx:1.27-alpine
Title: Image nginx:1.27-alpine is pinned by tag, not by digest
Description: Service "orders-api" uses tag "1.27-alpine", which names a moving target rather than one image.
Why it matters: A tag can be moved. That makes the deployment unreproducible in the direction that matters: rolling back to "the version that worked" pulls whatever the tag points at today, and two hosts deployed a week apart from the same file are not running the same software.
What to do: Pin nginx by digest (image@sha256:…) once you have the version you want.

Title: Registry reachability was not checked
Description: The deployment pulls from docker.io. This audit does not open outbound connections unless asked, so whether this host can reach them is unknown.
Why it matters: A host behind an egress firewall passes every other check in this report and then fails at the pull. This line is here so that outcome is not a surprise.
What to do: Re-run with --egress to test reachability, or confirm outbound access to those registries by other means.
